# Host <-> MCU protocol (generated)

<!-- Generated by protocol/gen from protocol/host (the computer <-> MCU USB protocol): do not edit, regenerate. -->

How a computer on the speaker's USB port talks to our MCU firmware: typed messages over control transfers to a
vendor interface. Defined in `protocol/host/src/lib.rs` (its header comment explains the transport): the MCU's C
(`mcu/src/zd1host_gen.h`) is generated from it; the computer's side uses the crate itself (`host/core`: the `zd1`
command line and the web page).

Protocol version 3. USB: 03EB:2FE0, the vendor interface of class FF/5A/01 (interface 3 in our firmware; hosts find
it by its class, its number moves with the interfaces before it). Requests (vendor, to the interface): CALL 0x01 (OUT, `wValue` = sequence number, one request), POLL 0x02 (IN, up to 512 bytes of
records: kind, u16 length, payload; 1 = log text, 2 = reply = u16 sequence number + message, 3 = the module's console's
bytes, while `Console` has it open), HELLO 0x03 (IN, `HelloReply`, answered from the interrupt). Messages are at most 256 bytes: id, then the fields in order,
little-endian; `str` = u8 length + bytes, `bytes` = u16 length + bytes. Any request may be answered with `Error`. Bulk data (`Pipe`) goes to the interface's one endpoint, bulk OUT 0x05, 64-byte packets; the MCU NAKs while its buffers are full.

## Compatibility

Firmware and tools of different ages meet, so the protocol only grows: an id is never reused, a message gains fields only
at its end, a field never changes its type or maximum. A decoder ignores bytes after the fields it knows (a newer
peer's) and leaves fields a shorter message doesn't reach at zero / false / empty (an older peer's); a field cut in the
middle or a length over its maximum is an error. `HelloReply.requests` lists the firmware's requests; an unknown one
gets `Error UNKNOWN`. `protocol/host/spec.lock` records every message and field there has been: `protocol/gen` refuses
a change that breaks these rules unless run with `--break`, which needs a new protocol version. Across versions the
base layer holds: HELLO (from the interrupt) and `Dfu` (id 0x06, unchanged since version 1), so a tool of any version
can put a firmware of any version into the bootloader and flash it; a tool refuses every other request to a firmware
of another version.

## The gate

Requests marked gated change the speaker (or read its RAM). With the gate locked they get `Error LOCKED`; `Unlock`
waits up to 30 s for a press of ON/OFF on the speaker (its LED flashes purple; the press does nothing else), after
which gated requests run until 10 minutes after the last one. A firmware's first start after it was flashed (its version
isn't the one the EEPROM recorded) is unlocked the same way: whoever could flash it could change anything already, and
an install goes on without a press. `Lock` closes it, or opens it for good (kept in the
EEPROM, for a unit tools drive unattended). The device can't tell which program or web page is talking to it: the
press is its own check. `zd1` and the web page ask for the press and unlock by themselves when a request needs it.

## Requests

The host's timeout is the request's own: the MCU answers within it, or the host gives up.

## The module's records

Encoded by the module OS with this codec, relayed by the MCU (`ModRecord`), decoded by the host: the MCU's C has none of them. A field marked set is a setting (docs/module/settings.md): the host writes it with `SetSetting`, the key the field's name with dots for underscores, the value in its string form (bools `on` / `off`, enums by name); the module checks it against the type, the maximum and the format.

### State (0x60)
The speaker as the module OS knows it: its settings (the fields marked set: written with `SetSetting`, the key the field's name with dots for underscores, the value in string form; kept on the data partition) and its status. The module pushes it when anything changes (once a second at most) and after every hello; the MCU keeps the last copy (`ModRecord State`). The same record, as JSON, is what an API on the module would serve.

| Field | Type | Setting | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | str <= 63 | `name` | the speaker's name: AirPlay, Spotify Connect, Snapcast and the MCU's device name; empty: "Zeppelin Air XXXXXX" from the MAC |
| `eth_mode` | [NetMode](#netmode) | `eth.mode`, default `dhcp` | the wired interface: off, DHCP (169.254.1.1 until a lease comes), or the fixed address |

| `stamp_b` | str <= 64 |  | the same for slot B |

### ScanEntry (0x61)
A Wi-Fi network seen by the module's radio (the `Scan` record, one entry per SSID; hidden networks are left out).

| Field | Type | Setting | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ssid` | str <= 32 |  |  |
| `signal` | u8 |  | its signal, -dBm (57 = -57 dBm) |
| `security` | [WifiSecurity](#wifisecurity) |  |  |

### KnownNetwork (0x62)
A Wi-Fi network the speaker knows (the `Networks` record, in the order it prefers them). Its key never leaves the speaker.

| Field | Type | Setting | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ssid` | str <= 32 |  |  |
| `security` | [WifiSecurity](#wifisecurity) |  | OPEN, or PSK: a WPA2 key is stored |

### Snapserver (0x63)
A snapserver found over mDNS (the `Servers` record): `snapcast.server` takes `host:port`.

| Field | Type | Setting | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | str <= 63 |  | its instance name (snapserver's: usually the host's name) |
| `host` | str <= 15 |  | its IPv4 address |
| `port` | u16 |  | its stream port (1704 unless it says otherwise) |

### Pairing (0x64)
A controller paired with the AirPlay receiver (the `Pairings` record).

| Field | Type | Setting | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | str <= 63 |  | the controller's pairing identifier (a UUID-like string its sender chose) |
| `admin` | bool |  | it may add and remove pairings |

### Actions (0x65)
The module OS's actions: writes with no state of their own (`SetSetting` with the key the field's name with dots for underscores; read back empty, or `!` and why the module refused). Not part of `State`.

| Field | Type | Setting | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wifi_add` | str <= 102 | `wifi.add`, network | join a network: added (or its key changed) and put first: `wpa2 KEY SSID` (KEY: its WPA2 key, 64 hex digits, derived from the passphrase on the computer) or `open SSID` |
| `wifi_forget` | str <= 32 | `wifi.forget`, ssid | forget a known network: its SSID |
| `wifi_first` | str <= 32 | `wifi.first`, ssid | put a known network first (the speaker prefers it when it sees both): its SSID |
| `airplay_forget` | str <= 8 | `airplay.forget` | forget every controller paired with AirPlay (any value): senders pair again; the accessory stays the same |
| `reset` | str <= 8 | `reset`, reset | back to the defaults: `settings` (every setting; the networks and AirPlay's pairings stay) or `all` (those too: as from the factory, but for the software) |

## Enums

### Err
Why a request failed (`Error.code`).

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | UNKNOWN | not a request this firmware knows |
| 2 | MALFORMED | the fields don't decode |
| 3 | BUSY | another request is running |
| 4 | MODULE | the network module is not up or did not answer |
| 5 | ARG | a value out of range |
| 6 | LOCKED | a gated request with the gate closed: `Unlock` first |
| 7 | DENIED | `Unlock` was not confirmed on the speaker in time |

### SysState
The speaker's state (mcu/src/source.h).

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | BOOT | starting |
| 1 | STANDBY | standby: do not disturb (only a person's key, pick, plug or play wakes it) |
| 2 | RUN | playing a source |
| 3 | ERROR | a protection tripped: amp off until cleared |

### Source
The selected source.

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | NONE | none |
| 1 | USB | USB audio |
| 2 | AUX | AUX in |
| 3 | WIFI | the network module |
| 4 | IPOD | the dock |

### NetMode
The network module, as the MCU sees it. How an interface gets its address (a setting per interface).

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | OFF | the interface stays down |
| 1 | DHCP |  |
| 2 | STATIC | the address, gateway and name server from the settings |

### WifiState
The Wi-Fi, as the module's supplicant reports it.

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | OFF | the radio is off (no supplicant: `wifi.mode` off, or no radio) |
| 1 | SCANNING | looking for the network |
| 2 | CONNECTING | associating, the handshake |
| 3 | CONNECTED | associated with `bssid` |
| 4 | WRONGKEY | the handshake failed: the key is wrong (shown through the supplicant's retries) |
| 5 | NOTFOUND | the network wasn't seen (until it is) |
| 6 | FAILED | the access point refused, or the attempt failed another way |
| 7 | IDLE | on, no network configured: the radio scans when asked (`Scan`) |

### WifiSecurity
What a Wi-Fi network's beacons offer, as far as this speaker can join it (`ScanEntry.security`).

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | OPEN | no key |
| 1 | PSK | WPA or WPA2 personal (a passphrase; WPA3 transition networks too): joins |
| 2 | SAE | WPA3 only (SAE): can't be joined (the driver's Wireless Extensions have no SAE) |
| 3 | OTHER | WEP, or enterprise (802.1X): can't be joined |

### Record
A record of the module OS (`ModRecord`): `State` is pushed by the module and kept by the MCU; others are made when asked. A list record is entries one after another, each a u16 length (little-endian) and a message.

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | STATE |  |
| 1 | SCAN | the Wi-Fi networks around the speaker: a list of `ScanEntry`, the strongest first, one per SSID; the module answers from its last scan and starts another (read again a few seconds later for it) |
| 2 | NETWORKS | the Wi-Fi networks the speaker knows, the one it prefers first: a list of `KnownNetwork`; it joins the first of them it sees (`Actions`: `wifi.add`, `wifi.first`, `wifi.forget`) |
| 3 | SERVERS | the snapservers on the speaker's networks: a list of `Snapserver`; the module answers from its last look over mDNS and looks again (read again two seconds later for it) |
| 4 | PAIRINGS | the controllers paired with the AirPlay receiver: a list of `Pairing`, the oldest first |

### ModState


| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | OFF | unpowered |
| 1 | RESET | powered, held in reset |
| 2 | BOOTING | powered, waiting for its status to say ready |
| 3 | READY | ready (status 0x2100): our OS, speaking this firmware's link protocol |
| 4 | UP | running, the link attached, the status not checked |
| 5 | STOCK | ready, but running the stock module software: no source (install ours, or restore the stock MCU firmware) |
| 6 | MISMATCH | ready, our OS, but its link protocol isn't this firmware's: the base layer only (update one of them) |
| 7 | BL2 | BL2 (status 0x2300) |

### ModOp
What `Module` does.

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | OFF | power off (reset, then the supply) |
| 1 | START | the boot-time bring-up, not waiting (off again after 180 s without ready) |
| 2 | POWER | power up and wait for ready (`timeout_s`), off again if it doesn't come |
| 3 | BL2 | power-cycle, HCR 0x21 at ready, wait for BL2 (status 0x2300) |
| 4 | HOLD | power-cycle and release the reset, nothing else: no SPI, no giving up (a JTAG session). State BOOTING |
| 5 | RESTART | off, then the bring-up (not waiting) |
| 6 | ESC | into BL2 through BL1's serial menu, whatever the module's image: power-cycle, then 0x02 on the console from the reset's release every 20 ms until BL1's menu is in, `4` CR once (nothing sent blind: the menu has "6) Erase Flash"); ok once BL1 says "Starting Bootloader Level 2" (BL2's web updater on 169.254.1.1 ~11 s later), not ok without the menu within 3 s. State BOOTING, as HOLD |

### Debug
The module OS's debug services (telnet shell, memory server).

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | DEFAULT | what the image says (`zd1.debug` on its command line: the debug image) |
| 1 | ON | on, until the MCU powers off or is told otherwise |
| 2 | OFF | off, the debug image included |

### Slot
What the module's boot stub starts (SPI reg 0xC4).

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | NONE | none |
| 1 | A | system slot A (NAND 32-64 MB) |
| 2 | B | system slot B (NAND 64-96 MB) |
| 3 | RESCUE | the rescue in the app partition: the MCU link and a shell, takes a system |

### BootOp
What `Boot` does.

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | TRY | start `slot` once, at the module's next boot: it becomes the good slot when the module gets ready with it, else the next boot is the good one again |
| 2 | GOOD | make `slot` (A or B) the good one |
| 3 | CLEAR | forget a try and the failures since the last ready |

### Sink
Where the bulk OUT endpoint's data goes (`Pipe`).

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | DISCARD | nowhere: counted and CRC-32'd (measuring the USB path) |
| 1 | MODULE | to the network module's updater over its console UART, as it grants it (`Update` sets it) |

### UpdateOp
What `Update` does.

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | BEGIN | start the module's updater: it takes `size` bytes from the bulk pipe into the slot that doesn't run |
| 2 | ABORT | stop sending; the module gives up on its own (10 s without data) |

### UpdateState
Where an update is (`UpdateReply`).

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | IDLE | none since the MCU started |
| 1 | STARTING | the module's updater was asked to start: waiting for its ready |
| 2 | STREAMING | the pipe's data goes to the module as it grants it |
| 3 | FINISHING | all sent: the module checks it and stamps the slot |
| 4 | DONE | installed: `slot` holds it (start it with `Boot` TRY) |
| 5 | FAILED | `text` says why; the slot holds no system |

### Key
A key on the speaker or the remote (`Key`).

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | ONOFF | ON/OFF, a short press: wakes from standby; in RUN, the next source (switched 1 s after the last press) |
| 1 | HOLD | ON/OFF held: standby |
| 2 | STANDBY | the remote's standby: toggles |
| 3 | VOLUP | volume up a step |
| 4 | VOLDN | volume down a step |
| 5 | PLAY | play / pause (to the USB host or AirPlay) |
| 6 | NEXT | next track |
| 7 | PREV | previous track |

### Play
The network module's play state, as its DRC XML says.

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | UNKNOWN | nothing heard yet |
| 1 | EMPTY | nothing queued |
| 2 | PLAYING | playing |
| 3 | PAUSED | paused |

### Player
Which of the module OS's receivers has the speaker (SPI reg 0xC6 b0).

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | NONE | none (or not our OS) |
| 1 | AIRPLAY | AirPlay |
| 2 | SPOTIFY | Spotify Connect |
| 3 | SNAPCAST | Snapcast |
| 4 | OTHER | another app |

### PlayerState
What that receiver does (SPI reg 0xC6 b1).

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | STOPPED | no session |
| 1 | PAUSED | a sender connected, paused |
| 2 | PLAYING | playing |

### DspIn
The DSP's input.

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | NONE | none |
| 1 | USB | I2S from the MCU (USB audio) |
| 2 | MODULE | I2S from the network module |
| 3 | AUX | the codec's ADC (analog AUX) |
| 4 | OPTICAL | S/PDIF (optical AUX) |

### Gate
The gate in front of the requests that change the speaker.

| Value | Name | |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | LOCKED | gated requests need `Unlock` (a press of ON/OFF on the speaker) first |
| 1 | UNLOCKED | confirmed on the speaker: open until 10 minutes after the last gated request |
| 2 | OPEN | open for good (`Lock` with open, kept in the EEPROM): for a unit tools drive unattended |
